section1.title: 1. Intro & Stats
section1.intro1: The Xiamen University Abalone Genetics and Breeding Team has conducted extensive research on abalone germplasm resources, aiming to explore and utilize abalone genetic diversity by analyzing different geographic populations, hybrids, and selected strains.
section1.intro2: Pacific abalone (Haliotis discus hannai) is the primary research species with 208,800 individuals, accounting for half of the total. It includes 7 geographic populations: Korean, Japanese, Dalian, Qingdao, Yangxia, Jinjiang, and Hainan, as well as 7 selected strains: high-glycogen, red-shell, purple-shell, high feed conversion, foot muscle pull, foot muscle color, and hypoxia-tolerant.
section1.intro3: Hybrid research is another highlight of our team. By combining advantageous genes from different abalone species, we have developed a series of new varieties. For example, green-disk abalone (H. discus hannai ♀ × H. fulgens ♂) and xi-disk abalone (H. gigantea ♀ × H. discus hannai ♂) and other hybrids involve a total of 57,000 individuals.
section1.intro4: Other abalone species including Haliotis gigantea, Haliotis diversicolor, Haliotis ovina, and Haliotis asinina total 47,900 samples. Research on triploids has reached 34,000 samples.

section1.title: 1. BenthicLab
section1.intro1: The Xiamen University Abalone Genetics and Breeding Team has conducted extensive research on abalone germplasm resources, aiming to explore and utilize abalone genetic diversity by analyzing different geographic populations, hybrids, and selected strains.
section1.intro2: Pacific abalone (Haliotis discus hannai) is the primary research species with 208,800 individuals, accounting for half of the total. It includes 7 geographic populations: Korean, Japanese, Dalian, Qingdao, Yangxia, Jinjiang, and Hainan, as well as 7 selected strains: high-glycogen, red-shell, purple-shell, high feed conversion, foot muscle pull, foot muscle color, and hypoxia-tolerant. These breeding efforts not only improve the success rate and economic benefits of abalone farming but also lay the foundation for subsequent genetic research.
section1.intro3: Hybrid research is another highlight of our team. By combining advantageous genes from different abalone species, we have developed a series of new varieties. For example, green-disk abalone (H. discus hannai ♀ × H. fulgens ♂) and xi-disk abalone (H. gigantea ♀ × H. discus hannai ♂) and other hybrids involve a total of 57,000 individuals. These hybrids demonstrate superior growth performance and environmental adaptability, bringing new hope to the abalone aquaculture industry.
section1.intro4: Other abalone species including Haliotis gigantea, Haliotis diversicolor, Haliotis ovina, and Haliotis asinina total 47,900 samples. Research on triploids has reached 34,000 samples.

policy.heroSubtitle: International frameworks, national regulations, and sustainable management strategies for the long-term conservation of abalone genetic resources
policy.intro: Abalone (genus Haliotis) are ecologically and economically important marine gastropods found in temperate and tropical waters worldwide. Due to overfishing, habitat degradation, disease outbreaks, and climate change, many wild abalone populations have experienced significant declines. A multi-layered policy framework — from international conventions to national regulations and local management measures — has been established to ensure the conservation and sustainable use of these valuable genetic resources.
policy.ctaDesc: Through collaborative research, sustainable aquaculture practices, and policy advocacy, we can ensure that abalone genetic resources are preserved for future generations.

iucn.title: IUCN Red List
iucn.desc: Many abalone species are listed on the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species. For example, Haliotis cracherodii (Black abalone) is classified as Critically Endangered, while Haliotis kamtschatkana (Pinto abalone) and Haliotis sorenseni (White abalone) are listed as Endangered. These assessments guide conservation priorities and resource allocation globally.

cites.title: CITES Convention
cites.desc: All species of the genus Haliotis are listed in CITES Appendix II (except for certain regional populations). This means international trade in abalone products requires permits and certificates to ensure sustainability. CITES trade monitoring provides critical data on global harvest and trade volumes.

national.title: National Protection Laws
national.desc: China classifies several abalone species under national and provincial wildlife protection laws. Marine protected areas (MPAs) have been established along the coastlines of Fujian, Guangdong, Shandong, and other provinces. Fishing seasons and minimum size limits are enforced to protect wild populations and spawning stocks.

sustainable.title: Sustainable Aquaculture
sustainable.desc: With over 95% of global abalone supply now coming from aquaculture, sustainable farming practices are essential. China leads global abalone aquaculture production, contributing to food security while reducing pressure on wild stocks. Integrated multi-trophic aquaculture (IMTA) systems are being developed to minimize environmental impact.

discus.name: Pacific Abalone
discus.status: Major aquaculture species; wild populations in steep decline

fulgens.name: Green Abalone
fulgens.status: California populations severely depleted; Mexico fishery managed

ovina.name: Sheep Abalone
ovina.status: Tropical species; low resources in South China Sea islands

asinina.name: Donkey's Ear Abalone
asinina.status: Tropical aquaculture species; important in Southeast Asia

gigantea.name: Giant Abalone
gigantea.status: Important for hybridization; wild populations threatened

diversicolor.name: Varied Abalone
diversicolor.status: Listed as CR in Vietnam Red Book 2024; key species in southern China

genetic.title: Genetic Conservation
genetic.desc: Establish cryopreservation banks for gametes and embryos of all major abalone species and their hybrids to preserve genetic diversity for future restoration and breeding programs.

monitoring.title: Wild Population Monitoring
monitoring.desc: Implement long-term monitoring programs for wild abalone populations along China's coastline, using environmental DNA (eDNA) and traditional survey methods to track population trends.

disease.title: Disease Management
disease.desc: Develop comprehensive disease surveillance and biosecurity protocols for aquaculture facilities to prevent pathogen spread between farmed and wild abalone populations.

climate.title: Climate Adaptation
climate.desc: Study thermal tolerance and hypoxia resistance across different abalone species and populations to identify strains suitable for future ocean warming and acidification scenarios.

cooperation.title: International Cooperation
cooperation.desc: Strengthen collaboration with regional partners (Japan, Korea, Australia, South Africa) on abalone conservation, sharing best practices for sustainable management and aquaculture innovation.

awareness.title: Public Awareness
awareness.desc: Increase public education and outreach about abalone conservation, sustainable seafood choices, and the ecological importance of abalone in marine ecosystems.
